title: Keeping Your Business Moving When the Network Wants to Stop
summary: Imagine it is a hectic Tuesday afternoon when, out of nowhere, a major regional public cloud provider goes down or a critical internet service provider
body_markdown:
Imagine it is a hectic Tuesday afternoon when, out of nowhere, a major regional public cloud provider goes down or a critical internet service provider (ISP) suffers an outage. Instantly, the internal corporate applications your team relies on every single day go dark. For thousands of remote and branch employees, productivity grinds to a halt. For your network security team, a high stakes fire drill begins. They are suddenly stuck trying to manage manual domain name system (DNS) overrides, emergency firewall adjustments, and attempts to revive decades old virtual private networks (VPNs) just to restore basic connectivity. It is an exhausting, expensive process that usually forces the company to temporarily fall back to broad, unprotected network access just to keep the lights on.


This isn’t a hypothetical horror story; it is the daily reality for organizations tethered to legacy connections or fragile, first generation zero trust network access (ZTNA) solutions. These older setups are built on rigid architectures that tightly bind the management plane to the data plane. If one piece of the infrastructure degrades, the entire access system collapses, taking business continuity down with it.


## A smarter approach to business continuity


Moving away from this reactive cycle means changing how your enterprise stays connected. As Andrea Bergamini, the Vice President of Global Infrastructure and CISO at Orbia,


[puts it:](https://www.netskope.com/resources/case-studies/orbia) “


*In just four months, we deployed Netskope technologies across 200 sites and 14,000 users without any business disruption. We provided security without compromising the performance of our business* ”. To achieve balance of security without performance trade-offs, Orbia migrated to


[Netskope One Private Access](https://www.netskope.com/products/private-access) , a universal ZTNA solution powered by the high performance NewEdge Network.


This approach achieves resilience by completely separating the management plane from the data plane. The system is built on a distributed, decentralized zero trust engine that operates locally right at the edge of the network. This means that even if a public cloud failure disrupts the primary management plane where policies are configured, your users never lose access to their applications. The platform delivers an industry leading 99.999% uptime and automated failover capabilities, eliminating the traditional bottlenecks and single points of failure.


## How decentralization saves the day


When network disruptions happen on the open internet (as they inevitably do), Netskope preserves business continuity through several advanced capabilities:


- Local authentication: Every NewEdge data center independently hosts inline authentication services so users always connect and authorize at the most performant location.
- Localized policy caching: Each data center maintains a real time localized policy cache for every single connected user, allowing zero trust rules to be enforced locally even if the main management plane goes offline.
- Smart traffic steering: The system continuously analyzes network latency and round trip times, bypassing ISP congestion by automatically rerouting users along the fastest, healthiest paths.
- Seamless failover: If a primary cloud broker experiences issues or goes down for maintenance, it is automatically removed from rotation, and the client instantly shifts to a fallback broker without requiring any administrator intervention.


## Unstoppable backup paths


True business continuity requires a fallback plan for extreme situations. Take connectivity as an example: Netskope Clients and Publishers reach the most performant point of presence (PoP) through a gateway selection service, not DNS. Only if that fails do they drop to standard DNS, which defaults to serving the nearest geographic point of presence. Users can also instantly switch to secure clientless browser access via the Netskope One Enterprise Browser or a standard browser to reach critical web, RDP, or SSH applications, all without needing IT help or admin rights.


To extend this resilience even further, organizations can deploy on premises business continuity options to supplement the cloud. For instance, you can run a virtualized local broker on your own infrastructure to enforce identical zero trust policies locally. You can also deploy a physical or virtual Netskope One SASE Gateway within your data center to establish an encrypted layer 3 tunnel, keeping users securely connected during widespread cloud outages.


Even better, if you are currently locked into a contract with another ZTNA provider, Netskope can be configured as a hot standby backup tenant. This allows users to safely cut over during an outage without needing to install a brand new agent ahead of time.


## Security and performance combined


Securing your business shouldn’t mean constantly bracing for the next connectivity crash. By embracing automated failover, intelligent path routing, and an architecture that handles disruptions gracefully, you can walk away from the era of network fire drills. You get a seamless user experience, guaranteed client stability through a strictly validated three month golden release cadence, and a network that keeps moving forward no matter what happens to the cloud around it.
